svg.aria-label: Three P2P attacks. Sybil: one attacker creates many fake peers that all connect to a normal peer; it can sway routing, search or voting and reduce reliability, and is mitigated by costly identity such as proof of work, stake or admission control, and by deriving node IDs from IP address ranges. Eclipse: attacker peers surround a target peer so honest peers cannot reach it; the target sees only malicious peers and can be fed fake data, mitigated by diverse peer selection, limits on connections per IP range and long-lived connections. Poisoning: a malicious peer sends corrupted data to Peers A and C and false routing entries to Peer B; it wastes bandwidth and spreads quickly, mitigated by verifying cryptographic hashes such as SHA-256, using multiple sources and majority checks, and reputation and incentives
